speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Inter-Ministerial Committee established to review Singapore's anti-money laundering regime will consider and study how potential offenders calculate (i) their own potential probability of being caught, (ii) the range of existing sentencing precedents, when proposing any tightening of regulations and enforcements to prevent exploitation by criminals; and (b) whether the Committee will consider recommending the enhancement of detection, investigation and sentencing to safeguard Singapore's stature as a respected financial centre.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Will the IMC in its deliberations also look at whether there is an increasing nexus of money laundering with organised crime, including organised cybercrime?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I raise this because there were media reports of a foreign national arrested in Singapore, following an extradition request.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: It was reported in the media that this foreign national faced charges, not just of money laundering, but also running a large-scale malware and botnet, relating to cybercrime.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And if there is an emerging nexus between money laundering and organised crime and other forms of crime, including cybercrime, will the IMC look at applying the full force of Singapore's policy levers, including the ones we apply to organised crime, today?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, money laundering and the methods employed by money launderers have become increasingly sophisticated.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They undertake multiple layering processes to hide their tracks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And obviously, with greater digitalisation, different categories of assets, it is becoming increasingly difficult to differentiate between legitimate and illicit fund flows.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I hope that helps address the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just a question for the Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Lately, over the last two years, in particular, there has been a term that is floating in the media lexicon – "Singapore-washing".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm whether the IMC will also be looking at the various permutations and aspects of some of the claims made by individuals and media organisations worldwide about how Singapore is potentially used as a conduit for such money laundering?
